name: origin-shifted-quiz-board
story: A centred four-answer quiz board drawn on a 1920x1080 document whose origin sits at the middle of the page, exported from Affinity's Export persona so the viewBox keeps the document's own signed coordinate space.
idioms: viewBox="-960 -540 1920 1080" - negative min-x/min-y with matching width="1920" height="1080"
xmlns:serif="http://www.serif.com/" with serif:id carrying the original layer name beside a hyphenated id
colours as rgb() inside inline style strings, and fill-opacity rather than opacity
identical rows drawn once at negative coordinates and repeated with transform="matrix(1,0,0,1,0,150)"
standalone="no" in the XML declaration, 4-space indentation
whyThisMatters: A fit-to-frame rule that reads only the viewBox's width and height, or measures a field's position from the raw x/y, puts this full-frame board half a screen up and to the left - the classic 'the artwork lands wrong' failure, and it never shows up in a sample whose origin is 0,0.
